basic_information.name: Milvus / Zilliz Cloud
basic_information.creator: Zilliz Inc. (San Francisco, USA / Shanghai, China) — Milvus is a Linux Foundation graduated project
basic_information.description: Milvus is a high-performance, open-source, cloud-native vector database designed for scalable approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search on massive datasets. Written in C++ and Go, it features a disaggregated compute-and-storage architecture enabling independent horizontal scaling. Milvus supports dense, sparse (BM25/SPLADE), and hybrid retrieval natively, with advanced quantization (RaBitQ 1-bit) and tiered storage reducing costs at billion-scale. Zilliz Cloud is the fully managed commercial offering built on Milvus, providing serverless, dedicated, and BYOC deployment options. With 40,000+ GitHub stars and 10,000+ enterprise production deployments including NVIDIA, Salesforce, eBay, and Airbnb, Milvus is the leading open-source vector database by adoption and scale.
basic_information.release_date: Open-sourced October 2019 under Apache 2.0; Milvus 1.0 March 2021; Milvus 2.0 January 2022; latest major version Milvus 2.6 released mid-2025
basic_information.license: Apache 2.0 (open-source); Zilliz Cloud is proprietary managed service
basic_information.github_stars: ~42,500 stars on GitHub (as of February 2026, surpassed 40,000 in December 2025)

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Cloud-native distributed architecture with four disaggregated layers: access layer (proxy), coordinator service, worker nodes (query/data/index), and object storage. Separates compute and storage for independent scaling. Supports three deployment modes: Milvus Lite (embedded Python library for prototyping), Milvus Standalone (single-machine server), and Milvus Distributed (Kubernetes clusters). Milvus 2.6 introduces Woodpecker, a zero-disk WAL system persisting logs to object storage (S3/GCS/MinIO), eliminating external message queue dependencies. Tiered storage automatically classifies data by access patterns (hot in memory/SSD, cold in object storage).
technical_architecture.language: C++ (core Knowhere search engine), Go (coordinator and distributed services); client SDKs in Python, Java, Go, Node.js, C#, RESTful API
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Supports up to 32,768 dimensions by default (configurable via Proxy.maxDimension parameter for larger dimensions). Optimized for common embedding dimensions: 384, 768, 1024, 1536, 3072.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: HNSW (primary for in-memory workloads), IVF_FLAT, IVF_SQ8, IVF_PQ, FLAT (brute-force), SCANN, DiskANN (for disk-based billion-scale), GPU_CAGRA, GPU_IVF_FLAT, GPU_IVF_PQ (GPU-accelerated), SPARSE_INVERTED_INDEX (for sparse vectors), BIN_FLAT, BIN_IVF_FLAT (binary vectors). Milvus 2.6 adds IVF_RABITQ with 1-bit quantization (1/32 compression) combined with SQ8 refinement achieving 95% recall at 1/4 memory footprint. Scalar quantization and product quantization also supported.
technical_architecture.scalability: Designed for billion-scale: horizontal scaling via Kubernetes with independent query nodes (read) and data nodes (write). Supports multi-tenancy via database-level and collection-level isolation. Sharding and replication for fault tolerance. Tested at billion-vector scale with BIGANN and LAION-5B datasets. 10,000+ enterprise production deployments validate production readiness at scale.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Milvus Lite (pip install, embedded in Python, ideal for Jupyter Notebooks/prototyping), Milvus Standalone (Docker, single server), Milvus Distributed (Kubernetes via Helm or Milvus Operator), Zilliz Cloud Serverless (fully managed, pay-per-use), Zilliz Cloud Dedicated (managed clusters), Zilliz Cloud BYOC (customer's cloud account). Available on AWS, GCP, and Azure Marketplaces.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector search (cosine, L2/Euclidean, inner product), native full-text search with BM25 (built-in tokenization, stemming, stop-word removal, on-the-fly scoring since v2.5), sparse vector search (SPLADE, BGE-M3), hybrid search combining dense + sparse vectors in same collection, multi-vector search with multiple query vectors. Score fusion via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, default with k=60) and Weighted Scoring for hybrid result merging.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Milvus is a storage/retrieval layer and does not impose chunking strategies. Integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Haystack for fixed-size, semantic, recursive, and document-structure-aware chunking. Zilliz Cloud Pipelines offer managed ingestion with automatic chunking and embedding generation. Users implement chunking via orchestration frameworks.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in hybrid search reranking with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and Weighted Scoring strategies for fusing dense + sparse retrieval results. Integration with external cross-encoder rerankers via LangChain and LlamaIndex. Multi-vector search supports ColBERT-style late interaction via separate vector fields. GPT-4o used as reranker in official multimodal RAG tutorials.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Full support for multimodal embeddings — any vector type can be stored and searched. Official tutorials for multimodal RAG with Visualized BGE (joint text+image embedding), CLIP (image search), and ImageBind (text-to-video search). Multiple vectors per record via separate fields enable storing text, image, and audio embeddings in the same collection. Named vector fields allow heterogeneous embedding dimensions.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No native knowledge graph engine, but extensive GraphRAG integration support. Official documentation for Graph RAG with Milvus (v2.6.x) including entity, relation, and passage collections for graph construction. Integration tutorials with Neo4j for GraphRAG agents (published August 2025). Cognee integration for automatic entity/relationship extraction and knowledge graph construction with Milvus as vector backend. LangGraph-based agentic RAG pipelines documented.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: No built-in citation generation or grounding verification. Milvus stores arbitrary metadata payloads alongside vectors (JSON fields), enabling storage of source URLs, page numbers, document IDs, and confidence scores for downstream citation generation by the LLM orchestration layer. Zilliz Cloud Pipelines provide document-level provenance tracking.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: No built-in context window management. Relies on orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack) for context selection, compression, and summarization. Milvus's efficient filtering, hybrid search, and reranking help select the most relevant chunks to fit within LLM context windows. Tiered storage and quantization optimize storage costs without affecting retrieval relevance.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Sub-100ms for typical RAG workloads on million-scale datasets. Milvus v2.2.3 achieved 2.5x latency reduction compared to v2.0. With RaBitQ 1-bit quantization in v2.6, memory footprint drops to 1/4 while maintaining 95% recall, further improving latency. DiskANN index enables low-latency queries on billion-scale datasets stored on SSDs.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: 46.33 QPS in comparative benchmark scenarios, reported as ~10x advantage over some competitors. 4.5x throughput increase from v2.0 to v2.2.3. Optimized batched search allows handling traffic spikes with minimal degradation. GPU-accelerated indexing (CAGRA, IVF) further improves ingestion and query throughput for demanding workloads.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: Configurable recall via index parameters (HNSW ef, IVF nprobe). IVF_RABITQ achieves 95% recall with 1-bit quantization + SQ8 refinement. Full-text search with BM25 uses on-the-fly scoring with TF/IDF for keyword relevance. Hybrid dense+sparse retrieval consistently outperforms single-method search in RAG quality benchmarks.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: Milvus official benchmarks use datasets from ANN-Benchmarks (SIFT-128dim, BIGANN, LAION-5B). Milvus v2.2.3 demonstrated strong scalability to billion-scale collections. On VectorDBBench (Zilliz's own open-source benchmark tool), Milvus/Zilliz Cloud led in low-latency comparisons. Independent comparisons show Milvus competitive with Pinecone and Qdrant, with strongest advantage at massive scale (100M+ vectors). Note: benchmark results vary significantly by configuration, dataset, hardware, and methodology.

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: LangChain (langchain-milvus package with vector store, hybrid search retriever), LlamaIndex (MilvusVectorStore with full-text and hybrid search), Haystack (MilvusDocumentStore), DSPy (MilvusRM retrieval module), LangGraph (agentic RAG pipelines), Cognee (knowledge graph + Milvus), RAG-Anything (multimodal RAG), and many more. Milvus Lite is the default connector backend for LangChain and LlamaIndex Milvus integrations.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Model-agnostic — works with any embedding model output. Built-in embedding functions in Milvus for OpenAI, Voyage AI, Jina AI, Cohere, and BGE-M3 models. Compatible with OpenAI (text-embedding-3-small/large, ada-002), Anthropic (via orchestration frameworks), Google (Vertex AI, Gemini), Mistral (mistral-embed), Cohere (embed-english-v3.0/v4), and all open-source models on Hugging Face (sentence-transformers, BGE, E5, CLIP, ImageBind).
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Official MCP server available at zilliztech/mcp-server-milvus on GitHub. Supports text search, vector similarity search, hybrid search, multi-vector search, and collection management via natural language. Compatible with Claude Desktop, Cursor, and any MCP-compatible AI agent. Supports stdio and SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport modes.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Apache Kafka connector (zilliz/kafka-connect-milvus on Confluent Hub) for real-time streaming ingestion. Airbyte connector for batch ETL from 350+ sources (S3, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, Salesforce, HubSpot, Notion, Confluence, Slack, Google Drive). Apache Spark connector for batch processing. Native support for bulk import from Parquet, JSON, and NumPy arrays. Zilliz Cloud Pipelines provide managed document ingestion (PDF, DOCX, HTML).
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Milvus exposes Prometheus-compatible metrics and supports Grafana dashboards for cluster monitoring (latency, throughput, resource usage). Compatible with LangSmith, Langfuse, and Arize Phoenix via LangChain/LlamaIndex tracing integration (OpenTelemetry). Zilliz Cloud provides built-in monitoring dashboard. Milvus 2.6 adds foundational audit logging capabilities. Langfuse cookbook available for LlamaIndex + Milvus Lite integration.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Open-core model: Milvus open-source is free (Apache 2.0). Zilliz Cloud uses consumption-based pricing measured in vCUs (virtual compute units). Tiers: Free (prototyping), Serverless (pay-per-use), Dedicated (reserved clusters), BYOC (bring your own cloud), and Business Critical (enterprise compliance). Storage priced per GB/month.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Zilliz Cloud Free Tier: 5GB storage, 2.5M vCUs/month, up to 5 collections, no credit card required. Additional $100 free credits on signup with work email (30-day expiry), plus $100 more with payment method (1-year expiry). Milvus Lite and self-hosted Milvus are completely free with no usage limits.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Serverless: $4 per million vCUs + $0.04/GB/month storage (standardized across AWS/GCP/Azure from January 2026). Dedicated clusters start at $99/month (standard) to $155/month (production). Data transfer at cloud provider cost, no Zilliz markup, with monthly free credits. Tiered storage delivers 87% storage cost reduction for cold data. Self-hosted costs are infrastructure-only.
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Self-hosted: free software + infrastructure (Kubernetes cluster costs vary by scale; a small deployment handling 1-10M vectors may cost $100-500/month in cloud compute). Zilliz Cloud Serverless: $0-50/month for low-traffic POC, scaling to hundreds/month at production scale. Zilliz Cloud Dedicated: $155-2000+/month depending on cluster size. Milvus 2.6 tiered storage and RaBitQ quantization reduce TCO by up to 50-70% compared to earlier versions. Embedding generation costs are separate (OpenAI ~$0.02-0.13 per 1M tokens, or free with open-source models). Key TCO advantage: no per-vector pricing unlike Pinecone, open-source avoids vendor lock-in.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in open-source vector databases. Highest GitHub stars (42.5K) among vector DBs, surpassing Qdrant (~28.7K), Weaviate (~15K), and Chroma (~18K). Over 10,000 enterprise production deployments. Positioned as the go-to choice for billion-scale vector search with heavy data engineering talent. Zilliz Cloud competes with Pinecone for managed vector database market share.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: NVIDIA (autonomous driving multimodal sensor data search, replaced FAISS), Salesforce (100+ internal tenants), eBay (e-commerce search), Airbnb, DoorDash, PayPal, Shopee, IBM, AT&T, LINE, Roblox (avatar search), Grab (food recommendation), Inflection. Over 300 major enterprises reported in production.
adoption_and_market.community_size: 42,500+ GitHub stars (as of February 2026), 600+ contributors. Active Discord community (primary chat channel since 2023, replacing Slack). Active on GitHub Discussions, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, and YouTube. PyPI pymilvus client actively maintained. Docker Hub milvusdb/milvus with millions of pulls. CNCF/Linux Foundation graduated project.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: $113M across multiple rounds (Seed through Series B extension). Series B extension: $60M (August 2022, led by Prosperity7 Ventures / Aramco Ventures). Initial Series B: $43M. Key investors: Prosperity7 Ventures, Temasek's Pavilion Capital, Hillhouse Capital, 5Y Capital, Yunqi Capital. No new public funding rounds announced since August 2022 as of February 2026. Valuation not publicly disclosed. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: Pinecone (fully managed, proprietary, zero-ops but higher cost and vendor lock-in), Qdrant (Rust-based, strong filtering and binary quantization, EU-based), Weaviate (Go-based, strong hybrid search, modular), Chroma (lightweight, developer-friendly, smaller scale). Indirect competitors: pgvector (PostgreSQL extension, simpler), Redis Vector Search, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch vector capabilities, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Vertex AI Vector Search. Milvus differentiates via: highest raw throughput at massive scale, most mature distributed architecture, largest open-source community, broadest index algorithm support, CNCF graduation credibility, and Zilliz Cloud as competitive managed offering.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Excellent for startups planning to scale vector search to millions or billions of vectors. Best fit: teams with some DevOps/Kubernetes capability (3-50+ engineers) building search, recommendation, or RAG products at scale. For early-stage startups (< 5 engineers), start with Milvus Lite (embedded Python) or Zilliz Cloud Serverless free tier for zero-infrastructure POC. Milvus Standalone (Docker) is viable for single-server production up to ~10M vectors. For startups needing true billion-scale, Milvus Distributed on Kubernetes or Zilliz Cloud Dedicated is the path. Cost-conscious startups can self-host on modest infrastructure. The open-source license eliminates vendor lock-in risk, a critical consideration for startup exit/acquisition scenarios.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Zilliz Cloud Serverless when: team < 5 engineers, traffic is bursty/unpredictable, budget allows pay-per-use pricing, fast time-to-market is priority. Use Zilliz Cloud Dedicated when: predictable production workloads, need guaranteed performance SLAs, compliance requirements (SOC 2, HIPAA via Business Critical plan). Self-host Milvus Standalone when: data sovereignty is critical, cost optimization matters (stable workload on dedicated hardware), single-machine scale is sufficient (< 10M vectors). Self-host Milvus Distributed when: billion-scale needed, Kubernetes expertise available, cost optimization at massive scale. Avoid self-hosting if no container orchestration expertise on team — operational complexity is significant for distributed mode.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 1-2 hours with Milvus Lite (pip install pymilvus, embed in Python script). MVP with RAG pipeline: 1-2 weeks using LangChain or LlamaIndex integration on Zilliz Cloud Serverless. Production on Zilliz Cloud Dedicated: 2-4 weeks including data migration, performance tuning, and monitoring setup. Self-hosted production on Kubernetes: 4-12 weeks including infrastructure provisioning, Helm chart configuration, monitoring with Prometheus/Grafana, and performance optimization. Attu GUI available for visual collection management throughout.
key_lessons: 1. Start with Milvus Lite for prototyping, then graduate to Zilliz Cloud Serverless — the embedded Python library lets you validate your RAG pipeline in hours without infrastructure, and the migration path to managed cloud is seamless.

2. Use hybrid search (dense + BM25) from day one — Milvus 2.5+ natively combines semantic and keyword retrieval in a single engine, significantly improving RAG accuracy without requiring a separate search system like Elasticsearch.

3. Invest in quantization early for cost control — RaBitQ 1-bit quantization (Milvus 2.6) compresses vectors to 1/32 of original size while maintaining 95% recall, dramatically reducing memory and storage costs at scale.

4. Don't over-provision infrastructure — start with Zilliz Cloud Serverless (pay-per-use) or Milvus Standalone, and only move to distributed Kubernetes deployment when your data actually reaches 10M+ vectors. Premature distributed deployment adds complexity without benefit.

5. Leverage the ecosystem — Milvus has the broadest integration coverage (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, DSPy, Kafka, Airbyte, MCP). Building on this ecosystem accelerates development and avoids reinventing data pipelines.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Attu is the official open-source GUI for Milvus (zilliztech/attu on GitHub). Provides visual collection management, schema design, data exploration, vector search, and system monitoring without writing code. Supports inline editing, smart filters, data import/export. Built-in text embedding functions since v2.6.0. Zilliz Cloud provides a web console with similar visual management capabilities. Neither is a full no-code RAG pipeline builder, but Zilliz Cloud Pipelines offer managed ingestion with minimal code.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — Build vs Buy decisions, infrastructure architecture) and Session 4 (AI business models & strategy — scaling costs, infrastructure economics, open-source vs managed trade-offs)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from official Milvus documentation (milvus.io), official PR Newswire press releases, Zilliz blog posts, GitHub repository (verified 40K+ stars milestone December 2025), Crunchbase/BusinessWire funding reports, and independent comparison articles.
confidence.cross_reference: GitHub stars milestone confirmed by PR Newswire, Yahoo Finance, and multiple news outlets. Funding ($113M total) confirmed by BusinessWire, PitchBook, TechTarget, and DealStreetAsia. Customer names (NVIDIA, Salesforce, eBay, Airbnb) confirmed across official Milvus use cases page and multiple press releases. Pricing confirmed via Zilliz official pricing page and AWS/Azure Marketplace listings. CVE-2025-64513 confirmed by NVD, GitHub Security Advisory, and multiple security outlets.
confidence.caveats: Benchmark results (46.33 QPS, 10x advantage) are from Milvus's own evaluation and may favor its architecture — independent benchmarks show more nuanced competitive positioning. Funding figures vary slightly across sources ($113M vs $115M vs $132M depending on which rounds are included). No new funding since August 2022 despite being 3.5+ years ago — could indicate revenue self-sufficiency or fundraising challenges. Distributed deployment has significant operational complexity compared to simpler alternatives like Qdrant or Pinecone. Zilliz Cloud pricing with vCUs can be opaque — actual costs depend heavily on query patterns and are hard to estimate without a POC.
confidence.security_posture: RBAC with fine-grained permissions at collection, database, and instance levels. TLS encryption in transit, bcrypt for credential storage. Milvus 2.6 adds foundational audit logging. Critical CVE-2025-64513 discovered in 2025: authentication bypass via forged sourceId headers affecting versions 2.4.0-2.4.23, 2.5.0-2.5.20, 2.6.0-2.6.4 (patched in 2.4.24, 2.5.21, 2.6.5). Zilliz Cloud (managed) provides additional security layers. Business Critical plan on Zilliz Cloud targets SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance. Elest.io managed Milvus is ISO 27001, SOC 2, and GDPR compliant. General vector DB attack surfaces (knowledge base poisoning, embedding inversion) not uniquely mitigated but access controls and network isolation reduce exposure.
